newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN FRIDGES, MOUTHES TO OPEN FOR BEN & JERRY'S.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN FRIDGES, MOUTHES TO OPEN FOR BEN & JERRY'S.

text.p: Tastebuds in Belgium could be tantalised this summer by Cherry Garcia, Wavy Gravy and Chunky Monkey as upbeat U.S. ice cream makers Ben & Jerry's Homemade Inc try to warm the cockles of Belgian hearts.
Under the banner "If it's not fun, why do it?" the $155 million company founded by Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield almost 20 years ago plan to make a dent in the Belgian ice cream market from May 5.

A selection of its 20 natural flavours, imported directly from the company's Vermont base, will hit refrigerators together with Ben & Jerry's social mission. The company donates 7.5 percent of earnings to socially-oriented projects.
Ben & Jerry's hope to break the ice mainly with vanilla- and banana-based creams. "The extravagant flavours will be left out," a spokeswoman for the company said. She gave no details.

She noted that in the Netherlands only nine of the palette totalling 50 flavours were for sale. The brand was launched there in 1996 and is currently available at over 300 outlets. In Belgium the aim is to have some 90 selling points.
The brand will be competing mainly with Haagen-Dazs, which falls in the same price category, but is aimed at a more upmarket, "tearoom", public, she said.

Belgium is the second Benelux country where Ben & Jerry's is being marketed after the Netherlands. Depending on the level of success in Belgium, the brand could be launched in Luxembourg in a year's time.
Elsewhere in Europe, it is available in France and the United Kingdom.
Details on the launch by the Nasdaq, New York, listed company are due at a May 5 news conference in Brussels.
